verdict.rationale: Browser Use has a public pricing page showing a credit-based, pay-as-you-go model ($5 minimum credits, no subscription, no expiry) and a one-time $15 signup credit with no card required, so there is some transparency before committing. The evidence never shows actual per-task or per-browser-hour rates, or any documented rate or concurrency limits. Missing for 10: explicit per-task/per-browser-hour unit prices, documented rate limits, documented concurrency limits, independent corroboration of pricing clarity.
